_notes: Augustinian career, second pool: the first house, the friends, the school and the college, the restlessness returning, the mission's letter, the offices (vocation director, formation director, novice director, school president, mission superior, prior, provincial). E3 §12, §14.

events.title: The First House's Table
events.body: The first house, and the table is the house: eight friars, a parish, a school down the road, and a supper at six that runs to eight since nobody leaves it, which is the order's way and this house's in particular. {@prior} has said, on the first night, that the house has one rule beyond the Rule, which is that nobody eats alone, and that the last curate broke it and is elsewhere, and has looked at you to see whether you understood.

choices.label: Be at the table every night, whatever the parish wants
choices.outcome: The parish wants a great deal and gets it from six to eight less, and notices, and the house notices the other thing, and the prior says at the year's end that you were a friar first and a curate second, which in this house is the order of things, and the parish forgives you by the second year.

choices.label: Be at the table most nights, and tell the prior when the parish needs you
choices.outcome: He says most is the number he had hoped for and that telling him is the whole of it, and the house is glad of you and the parish is too, and it is the arrangement every house you live in has after, since you learned it here.

choices.label: Ask him what the last curate did
choices.outcome: He tells you: a good priest who ate in the rectory office with the parish's books, and was a stranger in his own house in a year, and was moved at his own request, and is a good priest elsewhere and a lonely one, and the prior would rather you were not, and you are not.

events.title: The Weekly Letter
events.body: {@confrere} is in another house, four hours away, and the two of you have kept the thing the formation director said to keep: a letter a week, on paper, since the telephone is for emergencies and the paper is for the life. This week's is late and when it comes it is short and says he is fine and it is the first letter in three years that has said he is fine, which means he is not.

choices.label: Drive the four hours on your day off
choices.outcome: He is not fine. It is the house, which is not one, and a prior who is a good man and a bad prior, and he has not said it since it would be complaining, and you sit in his cell for an evening and he says it, and it is said, and he is a little better for the saying, and the letters are long again.

choices.label: Write a long letter back, and ask
choices.outcome: He answers in a page and it is the page he needed to write, and the letters are long for a month and then he is better, or the house is, and you learn that the paper can carry more than you thought, and less than a car.

choices.label: Telephone his prior, since it is an emergency
choices.outcome: The prior is startled and then, since he is a good man, grateful, and goes to the friend's cell that night, and the friend is angry with you for a month, and then not, since the prior was the one who could fix it, and did, some of it.

events.title: The School Down the Road
events.body: The parish school the house has run for ninety years is closing, or the diocese says it is, since the numbers are the numbers, and the parish has not been told, and the prior has been told and has told the house, and the house has divided into the men who would fight and the men who would not, and {@old_friar}, who taught in it for thirty years, has said nothing at all.

choices.label: Fight it: the parish, the alumni, the paper, the bishop's office
choices.outcome: It is a year of meetings and it works, for four years, and then does not, and the school closes anyway with the parish having fought, which the parish says was worth it, and the bishop's office says was not, and the old friar says, at the last Mass in the gym, that it was.

choices.label: Close it well: a last year that the children will remember
choices.outcome: The last year is the best year the school has had in a decade, since everyone knows, and the last Mass in the gym is the parish's largest in living memory, and the old friar preaches it, four minutes, and the children are in the front, and it is closed, and it was closed well.

choices.label: Ask the old friar what he would do
choices.outcome: He says, after a long time, that he would ask the children, and you do, in the gym, and they say the things children say, and one of them says the thing, and it is in the parish's letter to the bishop, and the school stays open, or it does not, and either way the children were asked.

events.title: The College Wants a Friar
events.body: The province's college has written to the provincial for a friar to teach theology, since the department is three laymen and the trustees have noticed, and the provincial has written to the prior, and the prior has said at supper, to the table, that it is you, since you have the degree, and that the house will be seven, and that he will say no if you ask him to.

choices.label: Go to the college
choices.outcome: The college is a different order: a campus, a department, students who are not sure why they are in the class, and a friars' house on the edge of it that is nine men and a chapel and is the best community you live in, since it is nine men who chose to teach. The department is four in a year and the trustees stop noticing, which is the goal.

choices.label: Ask him to say no; the parish is where the order is
choices.outcome: He says it. The college gets a layman, who is good, and the province's theology department is lay in a decade, and the college is the college and not the order's, and the prior says you were right for the house and the province says you were wrong for the college, and both are true.

choices.label: Offer two courses a semester, driving
choices.outcome: The college takes it, since two is more than none, and you are the friar in the department on Tuesdays and Thursdays and the curate the other days, and the students know you as the one who leaves, and the house as the one who is back, and it is six years of it and it is enough for the college to stay the order's, a little.

events.title: The Restlessness Returns
events.body: It has come back, as the formation director said, larger: not doubt, not desire, not tiredness, and all three, and it has come in the middle of a good year in a good house, which is the founder's joke, {@old_friar} says, since the restlessness does not come to the unhappy, who are busy. The friend is four hours away. The chapel is downstairs.

choices.label: Downstairs, every night, for the season
choices.outcome: The season is a winter. It changes as it changed before, from a weight to a shape to a kind of prayer, and it is larger this time and the prayer is larger, and the old friar says at Easter that you look like a man who has been somewhere, and you have.

choices.label: The four hours, on a Tuesday, without a letter first
choices.outcome: He opens the door and knows. It is an evening and it is the half of it he can carry, and you drive back at midnight with the other half, and it is lighter, and the old friar, who saw you go, says nothing, and puts a light on in the chapel.

choices.label: Bury it in the parish, since it worked last time
choices.outcome: It did not work last time, it turns out, since it came back, and it does not work this time, and it comes back a third time in a worse year, and the third time you go downstairs, since there is nowhere else, and it is the founder's joke, and it is on you.

events.title: The Lay Fraternity
events.body: There is a lay Augustinian fraternity in the parish, twenty people who meet on the first Thursday and read the Rule and have done so for thirty years, and their chaplain, an old friar of another house, has died, and their coordinator has asked the prior for you, since you said something at a funeral that she has written down and would like to hear more of.

choices.label: Take them, first Thursdays and the rest
choices.outcome: They are the most Augustinian people in the parish and the ones the friars have most neglected, and you learn the Rule from people who keep it in kitchens and offices, and the fraternity doubles in five years, and the province notices, and asks you to write about it, and you do.

choices.label: Take them, first Thursdays only
choices.outcome: It is enough for them and not for the coordinator, who wanted the rest, and the fraternity is what it was, twenty people on a Thursday, and is at your Masses, and it is a thing you did adequately and could have done well.

choices.label: Send them to the friar who has the time
choices.outcome: He has the time and not the sentence, and the coordinator writes to you at Christmas to say they miss what you said, and you go once, and then again, and are their chaplain in everything but the name by Lent, which was what she had in mind.

events.title: The Prior Is Tired
events.body: {@prior} is tired in the way priors get, in the fourth year of a term that has two more, and the house has noticed and has done what houses do, which is to be careful with him, and the carefulness is the thing that is tiring him, {@old_friar} says, since a house that is careful with its prior is a house that has stopped telling him things. You have a thing to tell him and it is not a small one.

choices.label: Tell him, plainly, as if he were not tired
choices.outcome: He listens and is, for the hour, not tired, since it is the first thing anyone has told him plainly in a year, and he says so, and does the thing, and the house learns from it, slowly, that he would rather be told, and the last two years are better than the first four.

choices.label: Wait for a better week
choices.outcome: There is not a better week, since he is tired, and the thing waits a month and is worse, and he says when you tell him that he wishes you had told him in the bad week, since it was bad anyway, and you learn that.

choices.label: Take it to the provincial, since the prior cannot carry it
choices.outcome: The provincial carries it and the prior hears that he did, and it is the thing that ends the term early, since a prior whose house goes to the provincial is a prior the province worries about, and he is moved, and is better elsewhere, and does not blame you, in words.

events.title: The Mountain Writes
events.body: A letter from the mission, from the old friar who has run it for thirty years and is not well, addressed to you since you were the student brother who came for a summer, or the deacon who said yes, or the friar the mission superior remembered, and it asks, without asking, whether you would come, since the mountain will need someone and he would rather it were a man who had seen it.

choices.label: Write to the provincial and ask to be sent
choices.outcome: The provincial sends you, since he was waiting for someone to ask. It is the mountain and the language and the old friar's last year and then his grave, and it is your mission after that, for as long as the body holds, and the body holds a long time up there, oddly.

choices.label: Write back that you cannot now, and might later
choices.outcome: He writes back that later is a thing men say and that he will be dead, and he is, in a year, and the mission gets a man from another province, and the letter is in your desk for the rest of your life, and you read it sometimes.

choices.label: Go for a month, and see
choices.outcome: The month is the month. The old friar is dying and knows it and shows you the mountain as a man shows a house he is leaving, and you come back and ask the provincial, or do not, and either way you saw it, and the old friar died having shown someone.

events.title: The House Votes on the Boiler
events.body: The Augustinian house votes on things, since the constitutions say it does, and this month the thing is the boiler, which is the parish's and the house's and will cost what the house has, and the prior has put it to the chapter, and the chapter is divided between the men who would fix it and the men who would ask the province, and the vote is even, and the prior has said he will not break it, since it is the house's.

choices.label: Vote to fix it, and say why: a house that asks is a house that is asked
choices.outcome: The vote carries by one. The boiler is fixed and the house is warm and poor, and the province, hearing, says the house should have asked, and the house says it did not need to, and it is the house's story for a decade, and you are in it.

choices.label: Vote to ask the province, and say why: it is what the province is for
choices.outcome: The vote carries by one. The province pays, since it is what it is for, and the house is warm and grateful and a little smaller, and the provincial says at visitation that the house knew when to ask, which is praise, and the old men do not think so.

choices.label: Abstain, and let the prior break it after all
choices.outcome: He breaks it, since he must, and the house is cross with you and not with him, and the old friar says that a friar who abstains is a friar who wants the house to decide without him and to blame him after, and it is unfair and it is a little true.

events.title: The Feast of the Founder
events.body: The twenty-eighth of August, and the house does what it does: a Mass with the parish, a dinner with the lay fraternity and the parish council and the pastor of the parish next door who is a Franciscan and comes every year to say the founder was a bishop and not a friar, and a speech, and this year the speech is yours, since the prior says the house has heard his.

choices.label: Speak from the Confessions: the restless heart, and what the house does with it
choices.outcome: The friars are moved and the parish is, mostly, and the Franciscan says afterward that it was the first Augustinian speech he had heard that was about the man and not the order, and comes back next year with a bottle, which is the Franciscan for approval.

choices.label: Speak about this house: what it has been, and who
choices.outcome: The parish is moved, since it is in the speech, and the friars are, since they are, and the old friar is named and weeps, which he does not do, and the prior says it was a speech for the house and that the founder would have approved, since he wrote a Rule for a house.

choices.label: Answer the Franciscan: he was a friar's bishop
choices.outcome: It is a joke and a good one and the Franciscan laughs and the table laughs and it is the shortest speech the feast has had, and the prior says it was the right length and the wrong subject, and the Franciscan says it was the right subject, and they argue, which is the feast.

events.title: The Friend Is Made a Bishop
events.body: {@confrere} is to be a bishop. The letter came from the nuncio and he telephoned you before he telephoned the provincial, which he should not have done and did, and he is not glad, exactly, since a friar made a bishop is a friar taken out of the house for life, and he has asked what you think, and whether he can say no, and he cannot, quite, and you both know it.

choices.label: Tell him to go, and that the friendship goes with him
choices.outcome: He goes. He is a good bishop and a lonely one, as they are, and the letters are weekly for the rest of his life and are the thing that keeps him a friar, he says, and you are at his consecration in the front, and he looks for you, and you are there.

choices.label: Tell him to try to say no, since a friar may
choices.outcome: He tries. The nuncio is courteous and does not accept it and he goes anyway, later and worse, since he tried, and the letters are weekly and he says in one of them that he wishes he had gone gladly, and that you told him to try, and it is a thing between you for a while.

choices.label: Tell him to telephone the provincial, and then you
choices.outcome: He does. The provincial says what provincials say, and then he telephones you, and it is the same conversation an hour later, and he goes, and says at the consecration lunch that he had wanted to hear it from you first and had, and had needed to hear it from the province second, and both were right.

events.title: The Vocation Director's Year
events.body: Vocation director, and the office is a car and a telephone and a list of young men who have written to the province, and a rule the last director left, which is that the order does not recruit, it welcomes, and that the difference is the whole of the office. The first young man on the list has written four times and been answered once, by the last director, and the letter said to wait a year, and the year is up.

choices.label: Drive to him, and see
choices.outcome: He is a good man in a bad town with a mother who does not want him to go and a pastor who does, and you sit in the kitchen with the mother for an hour and she does not change her mind and lets him go, and he is a novice in September and a friar for life, and the mother is at every profession.

choices.label: Write, and invite him to the house for a weekend
choices.outcome: He comes. The house does what it does with him, which is supper, and he is a novice the next September, and the weekend is the office's pattern after that: the house is the recruiter, and you are the man who drives them to it, and it works, mostly.

choices.label: Write that he should wait another year, since the last director thought so
choices.outcome: He waits, and does not write a fifth time, and is a diocesan priest in another state in six years, and a good one, and you read his name in a Catholic paper once and remember the four letters, and do not do that again.

events.title: The Formation Director's Page
events.body: Formation director, and the student brothers are yours: the union, the house, the renewals, and the page of answers the community gives about each man before the vote, which you have to read to him, since that is the custom you were formed under. This year there is a page with a line on it that would end a man, and the line is from a friar who is not reliable, and the man is a good one.

choices.label: Read him the page, the line included, and say who wrote it is not yours to say
choices.outcome: He hears it and is white and then is not, since you have said the second thing, and asks what he should do, and you say to be what he is for a year and let the house see, and he does, and the line is not on the next page, and the friar who wrote it does not write another.

choices.label: Omit the line; the page is the community's and the line is one man's
choices.outcome: The page is read without it and the vote carries and he never knows, and the friar who wrote it knows, and says at recreation that the formation director edits, which is true, and the next director reads everything, and you are not sure which of you was right.

choices.label: Go to the friar who wrote it, and ask him to withdraw it
choices.outcome: He will not, and says why, and the why is a thing about the student brother you had not known and should have, and it is not the line but it is something, and you read the page with the line and the something, and the vote is close, and carries, and it was the right page.

events.title: The Novice Director's Ninth Night
events.body: Novice director, and the house is the novitiate, and the ninth night has come as it comes: a novice weeping through a wall, and the silence, and the Rule, and you are the man at the door this time and the man who decides whether to go, and you remember which you had wanted, and the novice is nineteen.

choices.label: Go to him
choices.outcome: He is homesick in the way that is not about home. You sit with him an hour. It is the thing you wanted and did not get, or got, and it is right either way, and he stays, and says at profession that it was the ninth night, and you do not say that it was yours too.

choices.label: Keep the silence, and find him at breakfast
choices.outcome: You find him. It is enough, nearly. He stays, or does not, and you learn what the novice director knew, which is that the silence is a kindness too, some nights, and that the director who goes every time makes novices who cannot be alone, and it is a hard lesson and yours now.

choices.label: Send the socius, since it should be a friar and not the judge
choices.outcome: The socius goes and it is right, since the novice director votes and the socius does not, and the novice is easier with the socius after, and the socius says it was the best thing you did as director, which was to know what was not yours.

events.title: The Board Wants a Layman
events.body: School president, and the board has said, at its retreat, that the next president should be a layman, since the province cannot promise a friar after you and a school should not be built on a promise, and it is right and it is the end of a thing, and the board has asked whether you would say so to the province, since the province will hear it from you and not from them.

choices.label: Say it to the province: the school will be lay, and should be
choices.outcome: The provincial is quiet and then says he had known and had wanted a friar to say it, and the school is lay in six years and is a good school with the order's name and one friar on the faculty, and the province says you closed it, and the board says you saved it, and both are true.

choices.label: Ask the province for one more friar, and buy ten years
choices.outcome: The province finds one, since you asked, and it is ten years, and then the board says it again and the friar is old and it is a layman then, and the ten years were good ones, and the province says you asked for the right thing, and the board says you delayed it, and both are true.

choices.label: Tell the board it is theirs to say, and to say it
choices.outcome: They say it, badly, and the province is offended, and the school is lay in three years with the order's name and no friars, and the board says it was right and the province says it was rude, and you were in the middle, which is where a school president is.

events.title: The Mission Superior's Decision
events.body: Mission superior, and the mission is three friars and a mountain and a people, and one of the three, a young friar of the province in his second year up here, is not well: not the body, which is fine, but the thing the mountain does to some men, which is to make them small. He has not asked to go home. The province would take him home if you asked. He would never forgive it, or would.

choices.label: Send him home, and go down with him
choices.outcome: He does not forgive it for a year and then does, since he was small and is not, at home, and writes to say so, and the mission is two for a season and then three, and the province says you knew when to send a man down, which is the mission superior's whole job.

choices.label: Keep him, and take him with you everywhere for a season
choices.outcome: The season is a hard one and he is with you at every Mass and every burial and every walk, and by the end of it he is not small, or is small and useful, and stays, and is the mission's superior after you, and says it was the season.

choices.label: Ask him what he wants
choices.outcome: He does not know, and says so, and it is the first honest thing he has said in a year, and you decide for him, which is what he wanted, and send him down, or keep him, and he says either way that being asked was the thing, and it was.

events.title: The Prior's First Supper
events.body: Elected, and the house's first supper with you at the head of the table, and it is the same table and the same men and one of them is {@old_friar} who taught you the house and is now under you, in the constitutions' sense, and has said, going in, that a prior who changes the supper is a prior who has not understood the house, and you have two things you had wanted to change.

choices.label: Change nothing for a year
choices.outcome: The house is relieved and then, in the second year, ready, and the two things are changed then and the house says it was time, and the old friar says you were a prior who waited, and that the ones who wait last the term, and you do.

choices.label: Change one thing tonight, and say which and why
choices.outcome: The house hears the why. The thing is changed and is right and the old friar says that one is the number, and that priors who change two on the first night are priors who are asked to explain the second, and you did not have to.

choices.label: Change both; the house elected a prior, not a caretaker
choices.outcome: The house did, and says so, and the two things are changed and are right, and the old friar does not speak for a week, and then says the supper is better, which it is, and that he had not thought it would be, and it is a compliment with a wound in it.

events.title: The Friend Under the Prior
events.body: {@confrere} has been moved to your house, by the provincial, who thought it a kindness, and it is one, and it is also this: a prior with one of his three at the table, and a house that knows it, and a friar who has come to you on the second week with a thing he would like, which is a small thing, and which the house would notice, and which you would give to anyone else.

choices.label: Give it, and say at chapter that you would give it to any friar
choices.outcome: The house hears the sentence and watches, and you give the next friar the next thing, and the house stops watching, and the friend says the sentence was the right one and that he had not needed the thing, and had needed to know you would.

choices.label: Refuse it, and tell him why
choices.outcome: He understands, since he is a friar, and is a little hurt, since he is a friend, and the house notices the refusal as it would have noticed the gift, and the old friar says that a prior with a friend in the house will be wrong either way and should choose which way, and you chose.

choices.label: Ask the provincial to move one of you
choices.outcome: The provincial is puzzled and does it, since you asked, and the friend is four hours away again and the letters are weekly again, and the house says the prior was careful, and the friend says nothing about it for a year and then says it was right and he had hated it.

events.title: The House That Is Not One
events.body: Provincial, and the visitation has reached the house the province talks about: eleven friars, two of whom have not spoken in six years, and a prior who has stopped trying, and a parish that knows. The constitutions give you a week in the house and the authority to move anyone, and {@old_friar}, who was prior there once, has said the house was one in his time and that he does not know what happened, and that it might be him.

choices.label: Move the two, to two different houses
choices.outcome: They go. The house is nine and quieter and heals in a year, since the thing that was wrong was two men, and the two men are better apart, and the prior tries again, and the province says the provincial did the thing the last three would not, and the two men do not forgive you, and are friars.

choices.label: Stay the week, at the table, and say nothing about moving anyone
choices.outcome: The week is a week of suppers. The two do not speak to each other and both speak to you, and by Friday they have spoken through you, and it is not healed and it is started, and you leave the prior a page and the house a sentence, and the sentence is the Rule's first line, and the house knows it.

choices.label: Replace the prior, and leave the two
choices.outcome: The new prior is a good one and the two are the two, and it is two years before he asks you to move them, and you do then, and it is what you should have done in the week, he says, kindly, and you had known, and had hoped.

events.title: The Mission Question
events.body: Provincial, and the mission is the question: three friars on a mountain, all over sixty, a people who have had Augustinians for fifty years, and a province that cannot send anyone under fifty since it has nobody under fifty to send, and the council has asked whether the mission should be given to the local diocese, which has priests, and the mission superior has written to say he would rather die there, and will.

choices.label: Give it to the diocese, and go up to say so
choices.outcome: The three friars are silent at their table. One of them says the people will not understand and he is right and they do not, and the diocese takes it, and it is a parish then and not a mission, and the three come home, two of them, and the third dies there, on purpose, and is buried where he said, and the people come.

choices.label: Keep it until the last friar cannot stand
choices.outcome: The last friar cannot stand in six years and the diocese takes it then, unprepared, and the people are unprepared, and the three friars die on the mountain, as they wished, and the province says you were kind and the council says you were slow, and the people remember the friars.

choices.label: Ask another province to take it
choices.outcome: Another province has men and takes it, and the mission is Augustinian and not yours, and the three friars stay under another provincial and are glad, and your province has lost a mission and kept a mountain, and the council says it was clever, and the old men say it was a loss, and it was both.
